ios.desc:
This app is not intended for medical diagnosis or treatment. Always consult a qualified healthcare provider before making any health-related decisions. This app is for informational and tracking purposes only

Snap a photo of your blood‑pressure monitor—HeartLens logs it automatically, plus tracks weight & nutrition.

Blood Pressure Monitoring

Snap a photo of any BP monitor screen and HeartLens instantly extracts your readings. Works with Omron, Beurer, A&D, and virtually every device with a display.

Smart Food Tracking

Point your camera at any meal and get detailed nutrition analysis. AI identifies ingredients and calculates calories, protein, carbs, and fat automatically.

Weight Management

Log weight readings with date and time tracking. Monitor your progress with clear trends and insights.

Why HeartLens is Different:

- AI-Powered Analysis
Advanced image recognition reads BP monitors and analyzes food nutrition with high accuracy.

- No Bluetooth or Apps Required
Skip device pairing and manufacturer apps. HeartLens works offline with just your camera.

- Universal Compatibility
Supports any readable BP monitor screen and recognizes thousands of foods.

- Visual Health Trends
Track your progress over time with beautiful charts and personalized insights.

- Private by Design
Your health data stays secure on your device, with cloud backup.

- Simple, Modern Interface
Clean design with dark mode support makes health tracking effortless.

Whether you're managing blood pressure, tracking nutrition, or monitoring weight, HeartLens makes comprehensive health tracking simple and intelligent.

quotes.text: Anecdotal evidence: I found that it's super easy to eat way more than you should by just having some food laying around. And I don't mean just Cheetos - "healthy" food will set you back rather quickly as well. The amount of exercise doesn't matter that much - with the calorie density of common snacks, you will out-eat your exercise really fast. I don't think I'm that bad in that sense, but until I started keeping a track of what I eat and the count the calories, nothing worked. Yes it's a hassle, but I vibe-coded an app that does image analysis and tracks your calories. Shameless plug: HeartLens on app store, https://apps.apple.com/us/app/heartlens-your-health-tracker/id6747299126

quotes.text:
Built a small Flutter app called HeartLens that turns your iPhone into a pocket health kit: take a picture of your blood pressure monitor a BP reading, snap your meal for calories & macros, and quick-log water and weight. Everything syncs to Firestore (and Apple Health if you enable it) so your history’s backed up and shareable across devices.
It’s live on the iOS App Store (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/heartlens-bp-tracker/id6747299126). Would love feedback—accuracy vs a real cuff, food-detection fails, UI nitpicks, feature requests, anything. Cheers!
